question.text: The Aland [Oh-land]Islands, a Swedish-speaking archipelago forming an autonomous region of Finland, are found in this gulf, the northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. This gulf separates Finland and Sweden.
question.clue: To the west of Finland is this gulf and northernmost arm of the Baltic Sea. It contains the Aland Islands and serves to separate Finland and Sweden.

swap.leadin: These people ruled England from 1016 to 1035 under Canute.
swap.text: Name these Norse explorers and warriors who did not actually wear horned helmets.
swap.clue: A tax called these people's geld was paid following their victory at the Battle of Maldon.

question.text: This Northern European country had its neutrality broken when it was sold out to the Nazis by the traitor Vidkun Quisling.
question.clue: A parliamentary debate nicknamed for this country involved Leo Amery quoting Cromwell's command "In the name of God, go!", leading to the resignation of Neville Chamberlain.

swap.leadin: Sten Sture the Younger's dead body was burned at the stake during an event in this city.
swap.text: Name this city whose ruler Christian II led a "bloodbath" against heretics. Uppsala preceded this city as the capital of the Kingdom of Sweden.
swap.clue: The islands of Lidingo and Vaxholm are part of this city's namesake archipelago.

question.text: Canute was born a king of this non-Swiss country whose flag is a white cross on a red field.
question.clue: This country was defeated in one war after its adversary marched over a frozen strait to surprise its forces.

swap.leadin: He was given the epithets "The Golden King" and "The Lion of the North."
swap.text: Name this Swedish king who won at the Battle of Breitenfeld and died at the Battle of Lutzen.
swap.answerHtml: Gustavus Adolphus [or Gustav II Adolf; prompt on partial]
swap.clue: This man allegedly claimed that "the Lord God is my armor" before fighting without protection and dying at the Battle of Lutzen.

question.text: During its occupation, Norway was led by this Nazi collaborator. After the war, he was executed for high treason at Akershus Fortress.
question.clue: This man was appointed Commander of the Order of the British Empire for his humanitarian works, which included a stint in the Ukraine trying to help alleviate a famine there in 1921 undertaken at the behest of mountain climbing-humanitarian Fridtjof Nansen.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about history involving fishing.
swap.text: While attempting to repair a ship from this country's navy Halldor Hallfreðsson died during a fishing dispute. This country's Althing legislature threatened to leave NATO during a conflict with Britain over cod fishing territory.
swap.clue: A period of internal clan violence in this country is called the Age of the Sturlungs, and involved this country's great writer of sagas, Snorri Sturluson.

question.leadin: This leader brought meatballs to his kingdom after trying kofte during his exile.
question.text: Name this king who was joined by Ivan Mazepa in his retreat to Ottoman Moldavia. This king was carried on a stretcher to Turkey due to a foot wound that forced Count Rehnskjold ("RAIN-scold") to lead troops.
question.clue: In Estonia, eight thousand five hundred troops led by Carl Gustav Rehnskiold who assisted this ruler defeated thirty-seven troops led by Charles Eugene de Croy at one battle.

swap.text: Ruling from 1632 to 1654, this queen patronized Rene Descartes and eventually abdicated the throne to become a Catholic penitent in Rome.
swap.clue: This "Minerva of the North" who was tutored by Rene Descartes. Axel Oxienstierna served as an advisor to this monarch after the death of her father at the Battle of Lutzen.

question.leadin: Cowards die many times before their deaths: so, too, celebrities.
question.text: Reading his own obituary, in which he was described as the 'merchant of death', this man resolved to bequeath his wealth to the establishment of a series of prizes in various academic fields.
question.clue: This man bought the Bofors ironworks in 1894, transforming it into a prominent manufacturer of cannons.

swap.leadin: Christer Pettersen was convicted but later acquitted of this man's murder.
swap.text: Name this politician from the Social Democratic Party, a prime minister of Sweden who was killed in 1986 while walking home from the cinema with his wife.
swap.clue: This politician from the Social Democratic Party, a prime minister of Sweden who was killed in 1986 while walking home from the cinema with his wife

question.text: The Kalmar Union was founded by this monarch, who ordered that the False Olaf be burned with a necklace of his forged letters as kindling. The Victual Brothers were employed against this "Semiramis of the North" during her siege of Stockholm.
question.answerHtml: Margaret I of Denmark [accept Margaret Valdemarsdotter; prompt on Margaret]
question.clue: This ruler, who was often mocked as being "Pantsless" by Albert of Mecklenburg, was the first target of the Victual Brothers, who provided supplies to counteract this ruler's siege of Stockholm.

swap.leadin: Construction on this fortification began after the signing of the Treaty of Tartu in 1920, which established a border between two countries on the Karelian Isthmus.
swap.text: Name this defensive fortification constructed between Taipale and the Gulf of Finland.
swap.clue: Reinforced concrete and protection plates were dropped from this due to a rise in the price of steel, and parts of it were simply strategically placed mounds of soil known as "slope cuts."

question.text: Gerald Schoning's 1777 translation of Sturluson's Heimskringla posited the location of this site at L'Anse aux Meadows in Newfoundland. Leif Ericson allegedly settled this Viking colony in modern-day Canada.
question.clue: Etymological disputes over this place's name trace it to a word for pastures or, alternatively, to fermented berries or grapes.

swap.leadin: Answer these questions about the ways in which Vikings governed their territory after settling down from raiding.
swap.text: This Icelandic deliberative body, the world's oldest still-extant parliament, was established by Norse settlers in the 900s CE to resolve disputes.
swap.clue: It was disbanded in favor of the High Court from 1800 to 1845, when Christian VIII allowed it to reconvene.

question.leadin: A 1917 march praises the "strong arms" of a battalion from this country that carries a flag featuring a golden, sword-wielding lion on a red background.
question.text: Name this country whose Jager ("YAY-ger") Battalion consisted of troops trained in Germany during World War I.
question.answerHtml: Finland [or Republic of Finland; or Suomi or Suomen tasavalta or Republiken Finland] (The lead-in refers to the “Jäger March.”)
question.clue: Its two invasions by Russia were known as the Greater Wrath and the Lesser Wrath.

swap.text: The strike led this theater director, divorced single mother, and breast cancer survivor to run for President of Iceland; she served as the first elected woman head of state from 1980 to 1996. Please give her first name.

question.text: During the Thirty Years war the Heilbronn League was an anti-Catholic French-Swedish effort led by this Swedish First Minister.
question.clue: This man corresponded extensively with the Dutch merchant Samuel Blommaert ("BLOM-art") to set up a New World colony with his country's "South Company."

swap.leadin: The 1917 to '18 dispute over this territory is a textbook example of how the principle of self-determination shapes diplomacy in international law.
swap.text: Name this archipelago in the Baltic Sea that was the subject of a dispute between Sweden and Finland that ended with these islands of Swedes staying Finnish but becoming mostly autonomous.
swap.clue: In the 1920s, the League of Nations notably arbitrated Finland's dispute with Sweden over these islands in the mouth of the Gulf of Bothnia. The League found them to be over 90% Swedish in population, and thus naturally awarded them to Finland.
